construct.diagnosis_or_process: Pseudoachondroplasia is caused by dominant COMP variants; mutant COMP misfolds and is retained in enlarged rough-ER cisternae of growth-plate chondrocytes, disrupting chondrocyte function and cartilage matrix assembly.

source_verification.title: Pseudoachondroplasia/COMP - translating from the bench to the bedside
A novel form of chondrocyte stress is triggered by a COMP mutation causing pseudoachondroplasia

second_answer_attack.resolution: Activating FGFR3 variants cause achondroplasia and suppress growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation, but the stem gives a pathogenic COMP variant, normal craniofacial appearance, postnatal onset, and early degenerative joint disease. Pseudoachondroplasia specifically involves misfolded mutant COMP retained within rough endoplasmic reticulum of chondrocytes.

blind_audit.rationale: COMP is an extracellular matrix protein made by chondrocytes. Disease-causing COMP variants can misfold, accumulate within rough ER cisternae, retain interacting cartilage proteins, impair matrix organization, and promote chondrocyte dysfunction; this produces pseudoachondroplasia with postnatal disproportionate short stature and early degenerative joint disease. Strongest alternative resolved: Activating FGFR3 variants cause achondroplasia and suppress growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation, but the stem gives a pathogenic COMP variant, normal craniofacial appearance, postnatal onset, and early degenerative joint disease. Pseudoachondroplasia specifically involves misfolded mutant COMP retained within rough endoplasmic reticulum of chondrocytes.
